functions.name: Solution_Solve
functions.description: Executes the solution for the present solution mode (snapshot power flow by default). For a radial or meshed distribution feeder it runs the iterative unbalanced three-phase power flow, updating all node voltages, branch currents, element powers and system losses in the active circuit. Nothing is returned; results are read afterwards through the Circuit, Bus and CktElement accessors. Convergence must be checked separately via Solution.Converged.

return_info.description: Returns None. The solved state is stored in the active circuit and retrieved through result accessors (e.g. Circuit.TotalPower, Bus.Voltages).

examples:
import opendssdirect as dss
dss.Text.Command('Clear')
dss.Text.Command('New Circuit.demo basekv=12.47 phases=3 bus1=sourcebus')
dss.Text.Command('New Line.L1 bus1=sourcebus bus2=loadbus length=1 units=km phases=3')
dss.Text.Command('New Load.Load1 bus1=loadbus phases=3 kV=12.47 kW=1000 pf=0.95')
dss.Text.Command('Set voltagebases=[12.47]')
dss.Text.Command('CalcVoltageBases')
dss.Solution.Solve()
print('converged =', dss.Solution.Converged())

functions.name: Solution_Converged
functions.description: Boolean flag reporting whether the most recent Solution.Solve reached convergence. Called with no argument it returns True/False for the last solve; this is the canonical feasibility/admission check for a distribution power-flow task, analogous to inspecting the converged status of a transmission solver. A non-converged result (False) indicates the feeder did not settle within MaxIterations and any downstream voltages/powers are unreliable.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Optional override of the converged flag; normally omitted so the accessor acts as a getter of the last solve outcome.

return_info.description: True if the last Solution.Solve converged, False otherwise.

functions.name: Solution_Mode
functions.description: Gets or sets the present solution mode, which selects what Solution.Solve computes. Common modes are Snapshot (single power flow at the current loads), Daily/Yearly (time-series over a load shape), Direct (single non-iterative solve), and Fault/FaultStudy (short-circuit analysis). Setting Fault mode before Solve switches the engine from load-flow to fault-current computation, so this accessor is how a distribution study moves between the power-flow and fault-analysis task families.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: Integer solution-mode code (e.g. 0 = Snapshot, 1 = Daily, 2 = Yearly, 11 = FaultStudy). Omit to read the current mode.

return_info.description: Integer code of the current solution mode when called as a getter.

functions.name: Solution_MaxIterations
functions.description: Gets or sets the maximum number of iterations the power-flow solver will attempt before declaring non-convergence for a single snapshot solve. Increasing it can help stiff or heavily loaded feeders converge; if the solver hits this ceiling, Solution.Converged returns False. This is the primary knob for trading robustness against runtime in the iterative unbalanced solve.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Maximum iteration count for the snapshot power-flow solver. Omit to read the current limit.

return_info.description: The current maximum-iterations limit when called as a getter.

functions.name: Solution_Algorithm
functions.description: Selects the power-flow solution algorithm. Value 0 is the default Normal (fixed-point / current-injection) method that is fast and robust for well-behaved radial feeders; value 1 is the Newton method, which is more robust for stressed or meshed networks that struggle to converge under the fixed-point iteration. Choosing the algorithm affects both convergence behaviour and iteration count of the subsequent Solve.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Algorithm selector: 0 = Normal fixed-point, 1 = Newton. Omit to read the current selection.

return_info.description: Integer code of the currently selected solution algorithm.

functions.name: Circuit_TotalPower
functions.description: Returns the total complex power delivered into the circuit at the source, as a two-element list [kW, kvar]. By OpenDSS sign convention the values are negative because power flows out of the source into the loads. Taking the negated real part gives the total active power supplied to the feeder, making this the standard scalar extraction for a system-level power-balance or loss study after a converged Solve.

return_info.description: Two-element list [total_kW, total_kvar] of complex power delivered to the circuit at the source (negative by OpenDSS convention).

functions.name: Circuit_AllBusMagPu
functions.description: Returns a flat list of per-unit voltage magnitudes for every node (each phase of each bus) in the active circuit, ordered consistently with Circuit.AllNodeNames. return_info.description: List of per-unit voltage magnitudes, one entry per node, aligned with Circuit.AllNodeNames.

functions.name: Circuit_AllBusNames
functions.description: Returns the list of all bus names defined in the active circuit, in the internal bus order used by other Circuit-level array accessors. Buses are created implicitly by referencing them in element bus1/bus2 fields, so this enumerates the network's node set and provides the index/name mapping needed to interpret voltage and distance arrays or to drive Circuit.SetActiveBus.

return_info.description: List of bus names in the active circuit, in internal bus order.

functions.name: Circuit_Losses
functions.description: Returns the total losses of the active circuit as a two-element list [watts, vars] (note: watts/vars, not kW/kvar). This aggregates the series I^2*Z losses of every power-delivery element plus shunt losses, giving the single scalar most used to compare feeder efficiency across network-modification scenarios such as reconductoring, capacitor placement or reconfiguration.

return_info.description: Two-element list [total_watts, total_vars] of complex system losses in the active circuit.

functions.name: Circuit_SetActiveElement
functions.description: Makes a specific circuit element active by its full object name (class.name, e.g. 'Line.L1' or 'Transformer.T1'), so that subsequent CktElement accessors (Powers, Currents, Losses, Voltages) operate on it. Returns the zero-based index into the circuit's element collection, or -1 if the name is not found. This is the addressing step that precedes any per-element result extraction after a solve.

parameters.name: FullName
parameters.description: Full element name in 'class.name' form, e.g. 'Line.L1', 'Transformer.reg1', 'Load.Load1'.

return_info.description: Zero-based index of the now-active element in the CktElements collection, or -1 if the name was not found.

functions.name: Circuit_SetActiveBus
functions.description: Sets the active bus by name so that the Bus interface accessors (Voltages, puVmagAngle, kVBase, Isc, Distance) report values for that bus. Any node-list suffix is ignored. functions.name: Bus_Voltages
functions.description: Returns the complex phase-to-ground node voltages at the active bus as an interleaved list [re1, im1, re2, im2, ...] in volts, one complex pair per node present at the bus. return_info.description: Interleaved real/imaginary node voltages in volts at the active bus: [re1, im1, re2, im2, ...].

functions.name: Bus_Isc
functions.description: Returns the short-circuit (fault) currents at the active bus as an interleaved complex list [re1, im1, ...] in amperes, computed from the driving-point impedance at that bus. Requires Circuit.SetActiveBus first.

functions.name: CktElement_Powers
functions.description: Returns the complex power flowing into each conductor of each terminal of the active circuit element, as an interleaved list [P1_kW, Q1_kvar, P2_kW, Q2_kvar, ...] in kW/kvar. For a two-terminal line the first block is the sending-end injection; summing sending and receiving blocks yields the element's loss. This is the core per-element extraction for branch-flow, loading and loss analysis after Circuit.SetActiveElement.

return_info.description: Interleaved [kW, kvar] pairs, one per conductor per terminal of the active element.

functions.name: Text_Command
functions.description: Submits a single OpenDSS scripting command to the engine, e.g. 'New Line.L2 bus1=a bus2=b ...', 'Edit Load.Load1 kW=1500', 'Set mode=snap' or 'Solve'. This text DSL is the principal way to build and modify a network in OpenDSSDirect: elements, their parameters, and solution settings are all defined through command strings rather than Python kwargs. Errors are surfaced via the Error interface; use Text.Result to read any textual output of the command.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The OpenDSS command string to execute (a New/Edit/Set/Solve/Export/... statement).

return_info.description: Returns None when used as a command setter; any textual output is retrieved separately via Text.Result.

functions.name: RegControls_ForwardBand
functions.description: Gets or sets the voltage bandwidth (deadband, in volts on the PT secondary base) around the ForwardVreg set-point within which the active RegControl takes no tap action. A wider band reduces tap operations and wear but allows larger voltage excursions; a narrow band holds voltage tightly at the cost of more frequent tap changes.
